The results show that appropriately designed triggering rules preserve the essential optimization mechanisms of classical extremum seeking while drastically reducing the number of input updates. Numerical simulations demonstrate that comparable optimization performance can be achieved with significantly fewer actuation events, highlighting the suitability of the method for resource-aware digital and networked control implementations.
tldr: This paper presents an event-triggered discrete-time extremum seeking control framework for multivariable nonlinear systems, focusing on reducing actuation and communication effort.
motivation: Conventional discrete-time extremum seeking uses periodic updates, which can be inefficient. The authors aim to reduce resource usage by updating control actions only when necessary.
method: They combine discrete-time averaging with Lyapunov analysis to prove practical convergence and exponential stability of the average dynamics under event-triggered updates.
result: The proposed scheme achieves comparable optimization performance with significantly fewer actuation events compared to periodic implementations.
conclusion: Event-triggered extremum seeking is effective for resource-aware digital and networked control implementations.

title: Grazing Bifurcations Of Linear Impact Oscillators In The Zero Damping Limit
authors: David J. W. Simpson Olivia J. Goodman
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25229v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a harmonically forced linear impact oscillator, where impact events are instantaneous with energy loss. We study the dynamics at the grazing bifurcation of the non-impacting periodic solution in the limit that the damping coefficient of the oscillator is zero. Through numerical computations we show that a recurring sequence of bifurcations exists between points of resonance. Specifically, resonance creates a stable periodic solution that subsequently loses stability in a secondary grazing bifurcation, then regains stability in a saddle-node bifurcation, then transitions to a chaotic attractor through a period-doubling cascade. The dynamics persist under mild parameter variation, so apply to weakly-damped impact oscillators near grazing.
tldr: This paper studies grazing bifurcations in linear impact oscillators with zero damping, focusing on nonlinear dynamics and chaos.
motivation: Understanding the dynamics of impact oscillators near grazing bifurcations is important for mechanical systems with collisions.
method: Numerical computations are used to analyze the bifurcation structure as damping approaches zero, revealing sequences of bifurcations between resonance points.
result: A recurring sequence of bifurcations is observed: stable periodic solutions lose stability via grazing, regain stability via saddle-node, then transition to chaos through period-doubling.
conclusion: The dynamics persist for weakly-damped oscillators, providing insight into the behavior of impact oscillators near grazing.

title: Completing The Arakawa--Moreau Conjecture On Maximal Ideals Of Affine Vertex Algebras
authors: Sihai Jin
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25249v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Arakawa and Moreau constructed explicit singular vectors in a family of negative-level universal affine vertex algebras of types [MATH] and [MATH] and conjectured that the ideals generated by these vectors are maximal. Previous work established the [MATH] cases for [MATH], [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH], as well as the level [MATH] case for [MATH] with [MATH]. We prove all the remaining cases: the level [MATH] case for [MATH] with [MATH], and the negative-level cases with [MATH] for [MATH], [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH]. Together with the previously known results, this completes Arakawa--Moreau Conjecture 1. The proof determines the images of the prescribed singular vectors under minimal Drinfeld--Sokolov reduction and establishes simplicity of the reduced quotients by combining a Ramond--Zhu algebra argument, a Casimir-gap argument, and Li's spectral flow. Exactness and a nonvanishing theorem for the reduction functor then lift simplicity to the corresponding affine quotients. We also formulate a general maximality principle based on minimal reduction, give an alternative reduction-theoretic proof of the known level [MATH] result for [MATH], and obtain a rank-reduction proof of the maximal-ideal theorem for the collapsing family [MATH]. Consequently, every candidate quotient appearing in Arakawa--Moreau Conjecture 1 is the corresponding simple affine vertex algebra.
tldr: This paper proves the remaining cases of the Arakawa–Moreau conjecture on maximal ideals in affine vertex algebras, completing the classification.
motivation: The Arakawa–Moreau conjecture concerns the maximality of certain ideals in negative-level universal affine vertex algebras, which is a fundamental problem in vertex algebra theory.
method: The proof uses minimal Drinfeld–Sokolov reduction, Ramond–Zhu algebra arguments, Casimir-gap arguments, Li's spectral flow, and exactness/nonvanishing theorems for the reduction functor.
result: All remaining cases of the conjecture are proven, showing that the ideals generated by the prescribed singular vectors are maximal, and every candidate quotient is the corresponding simple affine vertex algebra.
conclusion: The conjecture is fully resolved, providing a complete classification of maximal ideals in these vertex algebras.

title: Proximal Gradient Methods For Unconstrained Set Optimization Problems With Set-Valued Maps Of Finite Cardinality
authors: Ravi Raushan, Debdas Ghosh, Anshika, V. Vetrivel
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25252v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work presents two different types of proximal gradient methods, with line search and without line search, for solving unconstrained set-valued optimization problems under the lower set-less ordering relation induced by a solid cone that is convex, pointed, and closed. The objective mapping of the problem involves finitely many functions, with each one being the sum of a continuously differentiable function and a convex function that is proper and closed. We present an approach to characterize weakly minimal points of the problem with the help of weakly efficient points of a family of vector optimization problems. Thereafter, we establish a stationarity condition along with its connection with weakly minimal points of the problem under study. Based on the stationary condition, the concept of a descent direction at a non-stationary point is discussed. In view of the line search-based method, we formulate an Armijo-type line search condition and establish the existence of such a step-size. For the proposed methods, global convergence is established under mild assumptions. The convergence analysis of the proximal gradient method with line search provides a theoretical advancement over the convergence results previously established for the steepest descent method in set-valued optimization problems. In addition, we analyze the computational complexity of the proposed methods and show that both methods achieve a convergence rate of [MATH]. Numerical results are reported to test the performance of the methods in practice.
tldr: This paper proposes proximal gradient methods for set-valued optimization problems, which is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: To develop efficient algorithms for solving unconstrained set optimization problems with set-valued maps, extending gradient methods to this domain.
method: Two proximal gradient methods (with and without line search) are introduced, using an Armijo-type condition and a stationarity condition linked to weakly minimal points.
result: Global convergence is established under mild assumptions, and a convergence rate of O(1/k) is achieved for both methods.
conclusion: The proposed methods advance set-valued optimization theory, but the work is purely in mathematical optimization and has no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Microsecond-Class Powered-Descent Optimization Via Exact Condensation And Strong Convex Regularization
authors: Wenbo Li, Ziqi Xu, Dai Shen, Shengping Gong
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25260v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fuel-dominant powered descent can be written as a convex program, but the usual full-state epigraph formulation still carries many state variables, fuel epigraph variables, and dynamics equalities. In addition, the pure-fuel objective provides no strong-convexity curvature. This paper combines three structural reductions. First, a dimensionally consistent low-weight energy term makes the control solution unique. Second, a terminal-state sensitivity recursion eliminates every intermediate state exactly; invertible row normalization turns the 30-node baseline with 300 primal variables and 174 equality multipliers into a problem with 90 control variables and six terminal multipliers. Third, the shared radial structure of the fuel norm and thrust ball gives an exact closed-form proximal operator consisting of group shrinkage followed by magnitude clipping. The condensed problem is solved with a fixed-budget extrapolated proportional--integral projected-gradient iteration implemented in fixed-size C17 arrays. In a Mars powered-descent case with energy weight 0.02 and relative reference-solution tolerance [MATH], the iteration count decreases from 2744 for the pure-fuel full-state epigraph baseline to 93, while the fuel metric increases by only 0.033\%. The mean end-to-end solve time is {\micro\second}, and P99 is {\micro\second}, on an Intel i7-10875H. Because the thrust set in this test case is already a convex ball, the contribution is fast solution of the convex core rather than a new lossless-convexification theorem.
tldr: This paper presents a fast convex optimization method for powered-descent guidance on Mars, using exact condensation and strong convex regularization.
motivation: To solve fuel-optimal powered descent problems quickly enough for real-time onboard computation on microcontrollers.
method: Combines a low-weight energy term for uniqueness, a terminal-state sensitivity recursion to eliminate state variables, and an exact proximal operator exploiting radial structure, solved with a fixed-budget projected-gradient iteration.
result: Reduces iteration count from 2744 to 93 with only 0.033% fuel increase, achieving microsecond solve times on an Intel i7.
conclusion: The method enables real-time convex guidance for planetary landing with minimal fuel penalty.

title: Sequential Preconditioned Conjugate Gradient Method For Linear Statistical Models
authors: Guan-Yu Chen, Dong-Yue Xie, Xi Yang, Zun-Hao Zheng
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25272v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a randomized iterative method for the ordinary least-squares estimation problem in large-scale linear statistical models, namely the Sequential Preconditioned Conjugate Gradient Method (SPCG). SPCG constructs a sequence of sketched least-squares subproblems with increasing sketch sizes, applies PCG as the inner solver, and warm-starts each subproblem from the previous solution. A final refinement stage is then performed on the full-scale problem. Since most iterations are carried out on smaller subproblems, the overall computational cost is significantly reduced. We establish the convergence theory, prove that SPCG attains OLS prediction accuracy, and derive per-subproblem iteration bounds and complexity estimates. Numerical experiments show that SPCG reaches the target prediction accuracy with fewer iterations and less CPU time than full-data PCG and Iterative Double Sketching (IDS).
tldr: This paper proposes a randomized iterative method for solving ordinary least-squares problems in large-scale linear statistical models.
motivation: Large-scale linear models require efficient solvers for ordinary least-squares estimation, but existing methods like full-data PCG are computationally expensive.
method: The Sequential Preconditioned Conjugate Gradient Method (SPCG) constructs a sequence of sketched least-squares subproblems with increasing sketch sizes, solves each with PCG, warm-starts from the previous solution, and finishes with a refinement on the full-scale problem.
result: SPCG achieves target prediction accuracy with fewer iterations and less CPU time compared to full-data PCG and Iterative Double Sketching (IDS).
conclusion: SPCG is an efficient algorithm for large-scale least-squares problems, with proven convergence and complexity guarantees.

title: On Weird Numbers With High Abundancy Index
authors: Kei Hisamoto
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25278v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let n be a natural number. It is proved that if the sum of divisors of n has sufficiently large relative to n, then n is some distinct sum of proper divisors of n.
tldr: This paper proves that if the sum of divisors of a natural number n is sufficiently large relative to n, then n can be expressed as a distinct sum of its proper divisors, relating to weird numbers.
motivation: Weird numbers are abundant numbers that are not semiperfect; the paper aims to characterize conditions under which abundant numbers become semiperfect.
method: The author uses number-theoretic arguments involving divisor sums and combinatorial constructions to show the existence of a distinct sum of proper divisors.
result: It is proved that for any natural number n, if σ(n)/n is large enough, then n is semiperfect (i.e., a distinct sum of its proper divisors).
conclusion: The result provides a sufficient condition for a number to be semiperfect, contributing to the classification of weird numbers.

title: Topological Stability In Paired Dynamical Systems
authors: Abdul Gaffar Khan, Pramod Kumar Das, Tarun Das
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25347v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the classical topological dynamical notions of shadowing and topological stability from a viewpoint of paired dynamical system [MATH], where [MATH] and [MATH] are uniform equivalences on a metric space [MATH]. We observe that if [MATH] is equicontinuous and commutes with [MATH], then the study of shadowing for [MATH] is reduced to the study of the classical shadowing for [MATH]. The fact that these assumptions are sufficient is justified through examples. Finally, we prove that if [MATH] is an expansive homeomorphism on a relatively compact metric space, then any pair [MATH] with shadowing is topologically stable.
tldr: This paper studies shadowing and topological stability in paired dynamical systems, which is a topic in classical topological dynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to extend classical notions of shadowing and topological stability to paired dynamical systems, where two uniform equivalences act on a metric space.
method: They define shadowing for a pair of maps and prove that under equicontinuity and commutativity, the shadowing property for the pair reduces to classical shadowing for one map. They also prove topological stability for expansive homeomorphisms with shadowing.
result: The paper shows that for equicontinuous commuting pairs, shadowing of the pair is equivalent to classical shadowing, and that expansive homeomorphisms on relatively compact metric spaces with shadowing are topologically stable.
conclusion: The work contributes to classical topological dynamics but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Learned Blockwise Port Activation For Real Time Beamforming In Fluid Antenna Arrays
authors: Yuanhui Wu, Zhentian Zhang, Hanjiang Hong, Hao Jiang, Zaichen Zhang, Kai-Kit Wong, Yin Xu, Wenjun Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25365v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fluid antenna arrays (FAAs), support multiuser downlink transmission by activating a subset of reconfigurable ports. The activation mask jointly determines the effective channel and the sparse radiating aperture, which requires a balance among sum rate, sidelobe suppression, hardware constraints, and online complexity. Channel driven selection can cluster active ports and increase sidelobes, whereas sidelobe oriented synthesis is typically channel independent and can sacrifice sum rate. This paper proposes learned blockwise port activation (L-BPA), for real time sidelobe aware FAA downlink beamforming. L-BPA activates a fixed number of ports in each aperture block, which supports grouped switching hardware and limits port clustering. A lightweight convolutional network scores ports using multiuser channel features, port coordinates, and user power statistics. Training combines blockwise straight through masks with a differentiable peak sidelobe level (PSLL), surrogate. During inference, learned scores are combined with multiscale geometric repulsion, followed by regularized zero forcing precoding over the reduced effective channel. L-BPA reduces the average PSLL by 3.26 dB relative to uniform sparse activation while achieving a slightly higher sum rate. It also reduces the PSLL by 8.13 dB and 10.10 dB relative to greedy and gain based selection, respectively, without iterative online search.
tldr: This paper proposes a learned blockwise port activation method for real-time beamforming in fluid antenna arrays, focusing on sidelobe suppression and sum rate optimization.
motivation: Fluid antenna arrays require efficient port activation to balance sum rate, sidelobe suppression, and hardware constraints, but existing methods either cluster active ports or sacrifice sum rate.
method: The authors introduce L-BPA, which uses a lightweight convolutional network to score ports based on channel features and user power statistics, combined with blockwise straight-through masks and a differentiable PSLL surrogate for training, followed by multiscale geometric repulsion and regularized zero-forcing precoding.
result: L-BPA reduces average PSLL by 3.26 dB over uniform sparse activation while achieving slightly higher sum rate, and reduces PSLL by 8.13 dB and 10.10 dB relative to greedy and gain-based selection, respectively, without iterative search.
conclusion: The proposed method enables real-time, sidelobe-aware beamforming for fluid antenna arrays with improved performance and low online complexity.

title: A Numerical Investigation Of The Rayleigh-Faber-Krahn Inequality For Polyhedral Domains
authors: Antoine Laurain Josu\'e D\'iaz-Avalos
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25419v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present numerical results for the problem of minimizing the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of the Laplacian among three-dimensional convex polyhedra with a prescribed number of facets. This problem can be viewed as a polyhedral version of the classical Rayleigh-Faber-Krahn inequality. Using a parameterization of polytopes by supporting hyperplanes, the problem is first reformulated as an equivalent finite-dimensional constrained minimization problem. A Lagrangian framework is employed for the numerical solution. Under the assumption that each vertex is incident to exactly [MATH] facets, the sensitivity analysis of the Lagrangian combines finite-dimensional perturbations of the facets of [MATH]-dimensional polyhedra with infinite-dimensional shape derivatives of both the eigenvalue and the volume. Depending on the number of facets, the numerical results yield well-known polyhedra, such as Platonic solids, prisms, and the tetrakaidecahedron, or reveal nonregular optimal shapes exhibiting several symmetries.
tldr: This paper numerically investigates the minimization of the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of the Laplacian among convex polyhedra with a fixed number of facets, a problem in spectral geometry.
motivation: The classical Rayleigh-Faber-Krahn inequality states that the ball minimizes the first Dirichlet eigenvalue; this work extends the problem to polyhedral domains, seeking optimal shapes among convex polyhedra.
method: The problem is reformulated as a finite-dimensional constrained minimization using a parameterization of polytopes by supporting hyperplanes, and solved numerically with a Lagrangian framework combining finite-dimensional perturbations and shape derivatives.
result: Numerical results yield known polyhedra (Platonic solids, prisms, tetrakaidecahedron) for certain facet counts, and reveal nonregular optimal shapes with symmetries for others.
conclusion: The study provides numerical evidence for optimal polyhedral shapes, contributing to shape optimization and spectral geometry.

title: Calabi-Yau Deformation Quantization
authors: Jakob Ulmer
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25438v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We record the Calabi-Yau version of Kontsevich's formality morphism from deformation quantization. As a special case we find that any unimodular holomorphic Poisson Calabi-Yau has a canonical closed deformation quantization of its resolved algebra of functions. A broader motivation is to find an explanation of Kontsevich's deformation quantization in the setting of Calabi-Yau categories via Sen-Zwiebach's string vertices.
tldr: This paper presents a Calabi-Yau version of Kontsevich's formality morphism in deformation quantization.
motivation: To extend deformation quantization to Calabi-Yau manifolds and connect with Calabi-Yau categories via string vertices.
method: Records the Calabi-Yau version of Kontsevich's formality morphism and shows that any unimodular holomorphic Poisson Calabi-Yau has a canonical closed deformation quantization.
result: A canonical closed deformation quantization of the resolved algebra of functions for unimodular holomorphic Poisson Calabi-Yau manifolds.
conclusion: The work provides a Calabi-Yau analogue of Kontsevich's quantization, with potential links to string theory and categorical structures.

title: Exact Discrete-adjoint Optimization Of Trap Timing And Placement In A Stieltjes-time Reaction-diffusion Model: A Galicia Case Study
authors: Iv\'an Area Francisco J. Fern\'andez
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25450v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Seasonal population models must combine diffusion, inactive periods and abrupt biological transfers while remaining differentiable with respect to localized interventions. We formulate a finite-dimensional timing-and-placement control problem for a Stieltjes-time reaction--diffusion model and derive the exact adjoint of the fully discrete residual. Continuous finite elements and an implicit Stieltjes--Euler scheme represent propagation, compartment replacement, resets and historical phase averages. For the resulting box-constrained penalized problem, we prove well-posedness and differentiability of the discrete control-to-state map, existence of a minimizer, first-order stationarity, and equivalence between direct-sensitivity and adjoint gradients. Benchmark tests show machine-precision agreement (below [MATH]) and adjoint speed-ups from about [MATH] to [MATH] as the number of traps increases from one to four. The method is applied to trap campaigns on a realistic Galicia mesh. Smoothed activation windows, domain-normalized moving kernels and the complete adjoint are independently verified. The final two-cluster control remains admissible and has a scaled gradient infinity norm of [MATH] with 120 temporal subdivisions per month. Fixed-control evaluations at 60, 120 and 240 subdivisions yield a refinement-increment ratio of [MATH]. At the finest level, the joint control outperforms time-only and reference controls, reducing the diagnostic objective by [MATH]. This reduction depends on uncalibrated trap-to-mortality intensities and should not be interpreted as field capture efficacy. The framework is fully reproducible, without claiming global optimality or a calibrated field-management prescription.
tldr: This paper develops an exact discrete-adjoint optimization method for trap timing and placement in a Stieltjes-time reaction-diffusion model, applied to a Galicia case study.
motivation: Seasonal population models require optimization of localized interventions like trap campaigns, but existing methods lack exact adjoint formulations for Stieltjes-time models.
method: The authors formulate a finite-dimensional control problem, derive the exact adjoint of the fully discrete residual using continuous finite elements and an implicit Stieltjes–Euler scheme, and prove well-posedness and differentiability.
result: Benchmark tests show machine-precision gradient agreement and adjoint speed-ups; the optimized two-cluster control outperforms time-only and reference controls, reducing the diagnostic objective.
conclusion: The framework is fully reproducible and provides a rigorous optimization tool for trap campaigns, though it does not claim global optimality or calibrated field efficacy.

title: A Criterion For Equidistribution Along The $\Omega$ Function Over Polynomial Sequences With Applications
authors: Cheng Zheng Zhi Qi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25454v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a certain fixed homogeneous polynomial of integral coefficients. In this paper, we establish a quantitative equidistribution criterion for the ergodic averages along [MATH]. Consequently, by an estimate of Lachand, we prove the following variant of a theorem of Bergelson and Richter: if [MATH] is an irreducible binary cubic form and [MATH] is a uniquely ergodic system with unique invariant measure [MATH], then for any [MATH] and [MATH], \lim_{N \rightarrow \infty} \frac 1 {N^2} {_{n_1, n_2 \leqslant N}} f \big( T^{ \Omega (|P (n_1, n_2)| ) } x \big) = \int_{X} f \ \mu . Moreover, we prove in the appendix a related conjecture of C\'espedes and Donoso over number fields.
tldr: This paper establishes an equidistribution criterion for ergodic averages along a polynomial sequence involving the Omega function, with applications to uniquely ergodic systems.
motivation: To extend equidistribution results to sequences defined by the Omega function (number of prime factors) over polynomial values, building on work by Bergelson and Richter.
method: The authors prove a quantitative equidistribution criterion using estimates from Lachand and apply it to irreducible binary cubic forms, also proving a related conjecture over number fields.
result: For uniquely ergodic systems, the ergodic average along Omega(|P(n1,n2)|) converges to the space average, with a specific rate for binary cubic forms.
conclusion: The work provides a new equidistribution result for arithmetic functions in ergodic theory, but is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Optimal Parameter Design For DIGing On Minimizing Unweighted Sum Of Squares
authors: Qiuchen Tian, Li Chai, Jinming Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: There is no general method for designing proper parameters to achieve faster convergence in distributed optimization algorithms. In this paper, we consider the distributed inexact gradient tracking (DIGing) algorithm with the objective function being the unweighted sum of squares. By representing the iteration algorithm as a dynamical linear system, we decompose it into different graph frequencies and obtain a set of decoupled subsystems, on which we can easily analyze the convergence rate. By using Routh stability criterion from control theory, we derive the explicit formula of the optimal worst-case convergence rate and the corresponding parameters. We can see that the convergence rate of DIGing is slow even for the simplest objective functions, thus acceleration is necessary for general application. The proposed method can be viewed as the first step toward optimal parameter design of DIGing algorithm in solving general objective functions.
tldr: This paper optimizes parameters for the DIGing distributed optimization algorithm to minimize unweighted sum of squares, using control theory to derive optimal convergence rates.
motivation: There is no general method for designing parameters to achieve faster convergence in distributed optimization algorithms, and this work aims to fill that gap for a specific objective function.
method: The DIGing algorithm is represented as a dynamical linear system, decomposed into graph frequencies to obtain decoupled subsystems, and the Routh stability criterion from control theory is applied to derive explicit formulas for optimal worst-case convergence rate and parameters.
result: Explicit formulas for the optimal worst-case convergence rate and corresponding parameters are derived, showing that even for simple objective functions the convergence is slow, indicating the need for acceleration.
conclusion: This work provides a first step toward optimal parameter design for DIGing in solving general objective functions, but the slow convergence suggests that acceleration techniques are necessary for practical applications.

title: Automated Numerical Stability Analysis Of Deep Learning Operators
authors: Xinye Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25494v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Finite-precision arithmetic unavoidably introduces numerical approximation errors. Numerical computations may use insufficient precision or an improper formulation, which leads to numerical instability. In this paper, we introduce the first unified software tool that integrates CESTAC for detecting the numerical stability of deep learning operators. Our developed software not only enables numerical validation with a single computation pass but also detects the sources of numerical instability and provides numerical stability monitoring during deep learning training and inference. We verified its effectiveness on the detection of polluted operators with injected numerical instabilities across various tasks. We believe that our developed method and tool provide valuable insights into developing numerically stable computing kernels, which are particularly critical for numerically stable and efficient deep learning training and inference.
tldr: This paper introduces a software tool for detecting numerical instability in deep learning operators using CESTAC method.
motivation: Numerical instability in deep learning can lead to inaccurate results, but existing tools lack unified detection and monitoring capabilities.
method: The authors develop a unified software tool integrating CESTAC for single-pass numerical stability validation, source detection, and monitoring during training and inference.
result: The tool effectively detects polluted operators with injected numerical instabilities across various tasks.
conclusion: The method provides valuable insights for developing numerically stable computing kernels for deep learning.

title: Construction Of Pbw And Canonical Bases In The Folding Extension Algebras For Symmetrizable Types
authors: Yumeng Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25495v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study extension algebras arising from Lusztig's construction of perverse sheaves on quiver representation spaces equipped with an admissible automorphism [MATH], leading to folding Khovanov--Lauda--Rouquier (KLR) algebras. Extending the method of M. Varagnolo and E. Vasserot to Lusztig's symmetrizable setting, we construct the skew group algebra [MATH], where [MATH] is induced by the admissible automorphism [MATH], and show that [MATH] preserves the signed basis and the crystal structure. In this framework, for finite types, we define standard and dual standard modules, analyze their behavior under dualities, and study the resulting Grothendieck groups. We prove that the transition matrix from the classes of indecomposable projective modules, which give the canonical basis, to the dual standard modules, which give the PBW basis, is upper triangular with diagonal entries equal to one. This provides a geometric categorification of these bases and of their relation in the symmetrizable setting.
tldr: This paper constructs PBW and canonical bases in folding extension algebras for symmetrizable types using geometric categorification.
motivation: To extend the construction of canonical and PBW bases to symmetrizable Kac-Moody types via folding of quiver representations with admissible automorphisms.
method: Uses Lusztig's construction of perverse sheaves on quiver representation spaces with admissible automorphisms to define folding KLR algebras, then applies Varagnolo-Vasserot's method to construct skew group algebras and analyze modules.
result: Proves that the transition matrix from indecomposable projective modules (canonical basis) to dual standard modules (PBW basis) is upper triangular with ones on the diagonal, providing a geometric categorification.
conclusion: The work establishes a geometric categorification of PBW and canonical bases in the symmetrizable setting, generalizing previous results for symmetric types.

title: Multimodal User Authentication Method Via Fusion Of Keystroke Dynamics And Glove-Based Hand Kinematics
authors: Lei Jing Issei Hyakuda
abstract: ArXiv:2607.24747v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Although keystroke dynamics are cost-effective behavioral biometrics, their practical deployment is hindered by susceptibility to environmental variations. To address this, we propose a robust multimodal authentication framework that augments traditional keystroke dynamics using 19-dimensional hand kinematics. Features are captured using a bespoke data glove equipped with 10 piezoresistive pressure sensors and a 9-axis IMU. A hybrid CNN-LSTM architecture effectively fuses these heterogeneous time-series streams. To ensure real-world applicability, we implemented a rigorous "unseen" evaluation protocol: the model was trained on a desktop keyboard using data from 1 target user and 8 "known" impostors, but evaluated on a laptop keyboard (cross-domain) against the target and an "unknown" impostor excluded from training. Averaged over five trials, the multimodal method achieved a mean Equal Error Rate (EER) of 2.12% for individual 600-ms authentication events (Window 1). Crucially, aggregating scores over 10 events (6 seconds) using a temporal smoothing window yielded perfect authentication (0.00% EER). While our ablation study showed IMU kinematics alone achieved equivalent performance in a static laboratory, error analysis confirmed that pressure and IMU sensors, despite strong physical correlation, possess distinct sensitivities to error factors. Fusing these modalities establishes a vital fail-safe against real-world vulnerabilities like spatial spoofing and environmental noise, highlighting that combined physical traits provide much stronger biometric discrimination than timing features alone.
tldr: This paper proposes a multimodal user authentication method fusing keystroke dynamics and glove-based hand kinematics.
motivation: Keystroke dynamics alone are susceptible to environmental variations; the authors aim to improve robustness by adding hand kinematic data.
method: A bespoke data glove with pressure sensors and IMU captures 19-dimensional hand kinematics; a hybrid CNN-LSTM fuses these with keystroke timing features.
result: The multimodal method achieves 2.12% EER for single 600-ms events and 0.00% EER when aggregating over 10 events (6 seconds).
conclusion: Fusing hand kinematics with keystroke dynamics provides stronger biometric discrimination and robustness against spoofing and noise.

title: The Missing Layer: Specification Infrastructure For Ai Oversight
authors: Saurabh Jha Satyam Kumar
abstract: ArXiv:2607.24866v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI safety has a missing layer. Interpretability, formal methods, security engineering, evaluation methodology, and reinforcement-learning safety each produce substantial work, but the resulting artifacts do not compose into deployable oversight: every team fielding an agentic system builds its own audit schema, policy dialect, monitoring stack, and escalation path, mostly reinventions of patterns understood elsewhere. We diagnose this as a coordination gap, not a research gap, and propose a two-axis taxonomy: five technical layers (Legibility, Specification, Mediation, Evaluation, Escalation) crossed with six concerns spanning alignment, robustness, adversarial defense, security, governance, and accountability, populating the resulting 5x6 matrix with existing work. Layer 2 (Specification), where humans translate intent into machine-checkable artifacts, is the connective tissue every layer depends on, yet it lacks four marks of a mature engineering discipline: shared vocabulary, design principles, composability standards, and governance practices. We propose six design principles for Layer 2, from elicitability and composability to adversary-awareness, traceability, and governability, made concrete through worked examples and a reference architecture turning specifications into runtime enforcement, evaluation, and escalation. Existing systems such as Cedar, Constitutional AI, and Open Policy Agent each address a fragment of Layer 2 well and the matrix poorly; treating them as fragments of one shared layer makes composition tractable. As evidence, we introduce CARMA, a Layer 2 prototype for autonomous ETL agents in which one specification drives enforcement, evaluation, and escalation, with every decision traceable to a versioned specification, naming what AI oversight is missing and giving independent teams principles to build the missing pieces so they compose.
tldr: The paper proposes a specification infrastructure for AI oversight, focusing on coordination and engineering discipline rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Current AI safety efforts produce artifacts that do not compose into deployable oversight, leading to reinvention of patterns across teams.
method: The authors introduce a two-axis taxonomy (five technical layers crossed with six concerns) and propose six design principles for Layer 2 (Specification), demonstrated through a prototype called CARMA.
result: The paper identifies a coordination gap and provides a reference architecture for composable specification, enforcement, evaluation, and escalation.
conclusion: Treating existing systems as fragments of a shared specification layer makes composition tractable and enables independent teams to build interoperable oversight components.

title: Trusting-Trust Attack Against An Entire Linux Distribution Through Binary Manipulation
authors: Julien Malka, Aman Sharma, Martin Monperrus, Stefano Zacchiroli, Th\'eo Zimmermann
abstract: ArXiv:2607.24888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ken Thompson's trusting-trust attack, in which a compromised compiler backdoors the programs it builds and reproduces the backdoor in subsequent rebuilds of itself, is widely regarded as a threat specific to compilers. We show that it is not. We construct a complete trusting-trust attack around GNU strip, an ordinary build utility that neither inspects nor generates source code, using only manipulations of finished ELF files. In the bootstrap of the NixOS Linux distribution, a single tampered strip in the binary seed implants a payload that propagates from one generation of strip to the next and survives into the final standard environment after the seed leaves the dependency closure. On a real nixpkgs revision, the attack builds a complete graphical installer without failures and backdoors almost every one of its binaries, enabling arbitrary malicious behavior of the subverted packages.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a trusting-trust attack on a Linux distribution by manipulating the GNU strip utility, showing that such attacks are not limited to compilers.
motivation: To show that trusting-trust attacks can be carried out using ordinary build utilities beyond compilers, posing a broader security threat.
method: The authors construct a complete trusting-trust attack by tampering with the GNU strip binary in the NixOS bootstrap, causing the backdoor to propagate through subsequent builds.
result: The attack successfully backdoors almost every binary in a complete graphical installer of NixOS, enabling arbitrary malicious behavior.
conclusion: Trusting-trust attacks are not specific to compilers; any build utility can be exploited, necessitating broader security measures.

title: Early Detection Of Distributed Backdoors In Multi-Agent Llm Systems: A Characterization Study
authors: Diego Fernandez Arias, Dev Prashant Mistry, Ren Wang, Yibo Hu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.24893v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems can be attacked by a payload that no single agent ever holds in full: a poisoned tool hides encrypted fragments in its observations, spreads them across several agents, and an external step reassembles and executes them after the run. Per-step safety checks that judge each action in isolation may fail to recognize the complete distributed payload. We investigate how early such an attack can be detected while the run is still unfolding, and how robustly it can be caught once its most obvious cues are stripped away. We build a working instance on a hierarchical multi-agent system, run it under benign and attacked conditions across five language models and two task domains, and record when each fragment is injected and when the payload is assembled and executed. Detection is a race against assembly. Before the first fragment is injected, attacked and benign runs are indistinguishable; once injection begins, a prefix detector flags [MATH] of successful attacks with a median of five steps remaining and a [MATH] safe-run false-positive rate. Because assembly occurs only after the run, these alarms arrive in time to abort nearly every successful attack. We then measure how much of that warning rests on removable surface cues of the attack rather than on its distributed structure. Generic zero-shot and behavior-trained detectors provide almost no warning at all; the detectors that do work lean in part on removable surface cues, chiefly the ciphertext's length and entropy, and once the entropy cue is removed from the payload and the length features from the detector, detection arrives later and transfers poorly across domains, though a fine-tuned model recovers some of the loss.
tldr: This paper studies early detection of distributed backdoor attacks in multi-agent LLM systems, focusing on attack characterization and detection timing.
motivation: Multi-agent LLM systems are vulnerable to distributed backdoor attacks where a poisoned tool spreads encrypted fragments across agents, evading per-step safety checks. Early detection is crucial to abort attacks before payload assembly.
method: The authors build a hierarchical multi-agent system, simulate benign and attacked runs across five LLMs and two domains, and evaluate detection using prefix detectors, zero-shot detectors, and fine-tuned models, measuring detection timing and robustness.
result: A prefix detector flags 100% of successful attacks with a median of five steps remaining and a low false-positive rate, but detection relies partly on removable surface cues like ciphertext length and entropy; removing these cues delays detection and reduces cross-domain transfer.
conclusion: Early detection of distributed backdoors is possible but depends on surface cues; more robust methods are needed to detect attacks based on distributed structure alone.

title: Latent Stability Analysis Of Malware Representations Under Feature-Space Perturbations
authors: Ken Mcgarry Bamidele Ajayi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.24896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Static malware detectors are commonly evaluated using clean-sample metrics such as accuracy, F1, ROC AUC, and PR AUC. However, these metrics provide limited insight into how learned malware representations behave when feature vectors are perturbed, how close samples move toward uncertain decision regions, or whether compressed representations preserve security-relevant structure. This paper presents a latent-stability analysis pipeline for malware perturbation assessment in EMBER feature space. The pipeline compares full EMBER features, PCA-based compression, beta/denoising variational autoencoder representations, Mandelbrot-inspired escape-time descriptors, and a PINN-style latent-flow module. We define Latent Escape Divergence (LED) to measure changes in escape-time profiles under perturbation, and use PINNFlow-derived residual, velocity, risk, and gradient-shift metrics to characterize latent movement. Experiments are conducted on EMBER static PE feature vectors using 180,000 training samples, 180,000 test samples, and 240,000 holdout samples. Full EMBER features achieve the strongest clean classification performance with ROC AUC of 0.9962 and F1 of 0.9713, while PCA-64 is the strongest compressed baseline with ROC AUC of 0.9846 and F1 of 0.9347. The proposed VAE+Mandelbrot+PINNFlow representation does not outperform these baselines for clean classification, but it provides additional diagnostic value under controlled feature-space perturbation probes.
tldr: This paper presents a latent-stability analysis pipeline for malware detection under feature-space perturbations, using EMBER features and various compressed representations.
motivation: Static malware detectors are typically evaluated with clean-sample metrics that do not capture behavior under feature perturbations or proximity to decision boundaries.
method: The pipeline compares full EMBER features, PCA, variational autoencoders, Mandelbrot-inspired descriptors, and a PINN-style latent-flow module, introducing Latent Escape Divergence (LED) and PINNFlow-derived metrics.
result: Full EMBER features achieve the best clean classification (ROC AUC 0.9962, F1 0.9713), while the proposed VAE+Mandelbrot+PINNFlow representation provides additional diagnostic value under perturbation.
conclusion: The proposed representation offers diagnostic insights for perturbation robustness but does not outperform baselines in clean classification.

title: Typo: Instruction-Dense Visual Jailbreaks Against Commercial Closed-Source Image-Generation Models
authors: Meng Xie, Li Zeng, Hangtao Zhang, Xianlong Wang, Ziqi Zhou, Pengpeng Qiao, Zhetao Li
abstract: ArXiv:2607.24897v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent commercial image-generation models can generate high-quality images with readable text (e.g., posters, infographics, and manuals), attracting considerable attention. Yet we first show that this same capability also introduces a previously unreported safety vulnerability: these systems may refuse to generate harmful text directly, yet permit the same content when rendered as text within generated images, i.e., safety alignment does not reliably transfer from textual outputs to text embedded in images. In this paper, unlike existing visual jailbreaks against image-generation models, which primarily induce models to generate harmful visual objects or scenes, we introduce the concept of instruction-dense visual jailbreaks, in which image-generation models produce detailed, readable, and actionable harmful instructions within images. Such outputs can amplify harm because the rendered instructions can be readily read and widely spread. To instantiate this threat, we propose TYPO, a black-box framework that exploits this safety gap by automatically generating adversarial TYPOgraphy prompts, which covertly steer image-generation models to express harmful intent as highly legible, typographically structured text. Specifically, TYPO decomposes prompt generation into two channels: a textual channel for reframing the target intent, and a visual channel for specifying its presentation form. We formulate these two channels as a dual-channel textual-visual strategy space and optimize candidate strategy combinations through an adaptive combinatorial search. Extensive experiments across four commercial models (i.e., GPT-Image-2, Nano Banana Pro, Qwen-Image-2, and Seedream 5.0 Lite) show that TYPO substantially outperforms nine representative jailbreak attacks by 50.2% in ASR on average, while incurring an average query cost of only $0.04.
tldr: This paper introduces a novel jailbreak attack against commercial image-generation models by embedding harmful instructions as readable text within generated images.
motivation: Commercial image-generation models can produce images with readable text, but safety alignment does not transfer to text embedded in images, creating a vulnerability.
method: The authors propose TYPO, a black-box framework that uses a dual-channel textual-visual strategy space and adaptive combinatorial search to generate adversarial typography prompts.
result: TYPO outperforms nine representative jailbreak attacks by 50.2% in ASR on average across four commercial models, with an average query cost of $0.04.
conclusion: The work highlights a new safety vulnerability in image-generation models and demonstrates an effective attack, urging the need for improved safety alignment.

title: Alibi: Adaptive Agentic Attacks On LLM-Based Vulnerability Detectors Via Adversarial Code Comments
authors: Cristina Nita-Rotaru Zixuan Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.24964v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models are increasingly deployed for security-sensitive tasks such as vulnerability detection and code review. Their reliance on natural-language context embedded in source code exposes a previously underexplored attack surface: adversarial comments that can influence a detector's reasoning without changing program behavior. We study LLM-based vulnerability detectors against a new adversary: a coding agent that implements new functionality, deliberately introduces vulnerabilities, and strategically inserts adversarial source-code comments to evade detection. We present ALIBI, an automated adaptive black-box attack framework that generates and iteratively refines adversarial comments using detector reasoning and feedback. We transform real-world vulnerability-fixing commits into coding tasks and evaluate four representative LLM-based vulnerability detectors, ranging from specialized open-weight reasoning models to frontier multi-agent systems. All evaluated detectors are highly vulnerable: attack success rates exceed 90% across 125 real-world null-pointer dereference vulnerabilities, reaching 100% on one system. The framework also generalizes beyond this vulnerability class. Adversarial comments steering detector reasoning or fabricating external tool results prove most effective, while iterative refinement based on detector feedback further increases attack success. Finally, prompt-level defenses provide limited robustness against adaptive attacks, whereas architectural isolation and pre-detector comment sanitization substantially improve resilience. Our findings expose a fundamental attack surface in current LLM-based vulnerability detectors and motivate security-aware designs that carefully calibrate trust between natural-language context and program evidence.
tldr: This paper presents an adaptive black-box attack framework that generates adversarial code comments to evade LLM-based vulnerability detectors.
motivation: LLM-based vulnerability detectors are increasingly used for security tasks, but their reliance on natural-language context in source code introduces a new attack surface via adversarial comments that can influence detector reasoning without changing program behavior.
method: The authors develop ALIBI, an automated framework that iteratively refines adversarial comments using detector feedback, and evaluate it on real-world vulnerability-fixing commits against four representative LLM-based detectors.
result: Attack success rates exceed 90% across 125 real-world null-pointer dereference vulnerabilities, reaching 100% on one system; adversarial comments steering detector reasoning or fabricating external tool results are most effective.
conclusion: Current LLM-based vulnerability detectors are highly vulnerable to adversarial comments, and while prompt-level defenses offer limited robustness, architectural isolation and comment sanitization substantially improve resilience.

title: Zimpaf & RedPhuzz: High-fidelity Web Application Fuzzing Via Branch, Language Construct, And Function Call Monitoring
authors: Christoph Csallner Tennov Simanjuntak
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present ZIMPAF, runtime interpreter instrumentation, and RedPhuzz, a fuzzer, to address key limitations of state-of-the-art fuzzers: inefficient instrumentation, the lack of knowledge of the execution environment, and limited web domain knowledge. ZIMPAF implements a novel multi-granular runtime interpreter instrumentation that provides branch coverage, robust error and exception logging, function and language construct monitoring, and identification of user-supplied inputs used in branch instructions. The instrumentation is capable of identifying potentially vulnerable functions whose parameters are tainted, marking them as high-valued fuzzing targets, without performing taint analysis. It also employs a novel backward constant probe to infer potentially vulnerable functions whose parameters originate from constants, indicating their invulnerability and allowing them to be skipped. This information is utilized by RedPhuzz to perform highly-targeted function-and input-level fuzzing that goes beyond simple error-based fuzzing, but also detects silent vulnerabilities via multi-stage vulnerability detection. We also introduce three novel mutation strategies to achieve highly targeted and effective fuzzing: sanitization-aware, input-in-branch-aware, and data type-aware mutation. We evaluate RedPhuzz's performance with its predecessor (Phuzz) with 86 test cases across six benchmark web applications. RedPhuzz detects all vulnerabilities, while Phuzz fails to detect 16. RedPhuzz is 73% faster than Phuzz despite performing more tasks. ZIMPAF is faster than Phuzz's instrumentation (PCOV and UOPZ), while writing significantly more data. ZIMPAF achieves 2.1 to 41.22 times higher throughput than PCOV and UOPZ across five sampled benchmarks, and 0.87 times for one.
tldr: This paper presents ZIMPAF and RedPhuzz, tools for high-fidelity web application fuzzing using runtime interpreter instrumentation and targeted mutation strategies.
motivation: State-of-the-art fuzzers suffer from inefficient instrumentation, lack of execution environment knowledge, and limited web domain knowledge, leading to missed vulnerabilities.
method: ZIMPAF provides multi-granular runtime instrumentation for branch coverage, error logging, and function monitoring without taint analysis. RedPhuzz uses this information for targeted fuzzing with novel mutation strategies.
result: RedPhuzz detects all vulnerabilities in 86 test cases across six web applications, outperforming Phuzz which missed 16, and is 73% faster. ZIMPAF achieves 2.1 to 41.22 times higher throughput than prior instrumentation.
conclusion: The proposed tools significantly improve web application fuzzing efficiency and vulnerability detection, but the work is in software engineering and security, not quantum information theory.

title: An Attack On High Rate McEliece Cryptosystems Using Generalized Reed Solomon Codes With Weight $2$ Mask
authors: Julia Lieb, Abhinaba Mazumder, Michael Schaller
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25027v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Due to the insecurity of McEliece cryptosystems instantiated with Generalized Reed-Solomon codes, there have been several proposals of McEliece type systems that replace the permutation matrix by a matrix [MATH] with larger row and column weight. In many of them, the secret key is still a GRS code. There have been successful attacks on some of those schemes with row and column weight between [MATH] and [MATH], where [MATH] is the rate of the code. The case of weight two and larger has been left open in these works. Subsequently, several authors proposed schemes with weight exactly two and with even higher weight. We provide distinguishers for the public codes appearing in these cryptosystems in the high rate regime. In addition, we give a framework to turn a good enough distinguisher into a key-recovery attack. In the case where the matrix [MATH] has row and column weight [MATH], we can successfully attack the scheme in the high rate regime using a cube code distinguisher.
tldr: This paper attacks McEliece cryptosystems using Generalized Reed-Solomon codes with weight-2 mask, proposing distinguishers and key-recovery attacks.
motivation: McEliece cryptosystems instantiated with GRS codes are insecure, and previous attacks left the case of weight-2 mask open; this work closes that gap.
method: The authors develop distinguishers for public codes in high-rate regimes and provide a framework to convert a distinguisher into a key-recovery attack, specifically using a cube code distinguisher for weight-2 masks.
result: They successfully attack the scheme in the high-rate regime when the mask has row and column weight 2.
conclusion: The proposed cryptosystems with weight-2 masks are insecure, and the attack framework can be extended to higher weights.

title: An Artificial Market For Brazilian Real Estate Investment Funds: An Agent-Based Proposal
authors: Gilberto Gil F. G. Passos, Eber Assis Schmitz, Sildenir Alves Ribeiro
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25098v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article presents the development and validation of an artificial market for Brazilian Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs), known as Fundos de Investimento Imobiliario (FIIs), using agent-based modeling methodology. The central contribution of this work is the integration, within a single multi-agent system, of the FII value chain, from the generation of real estate revenues subject to vacancy and operational costs, through dividend distribution, to the trading of shares by heterogeneous investors mediated by a double auction mechanism with an order book. The model incorporates endogenous macroeconomic variables, such as the Selic, the Brazilian benchmark interest rate, and inflation, and represents agent heterogeneity through a behavioral decomposition into fundamentalist, speculator, and noise trader components, modulated by individual financial literacy levels. The model was calibrated using the Method of Simulated Moments applied to the historical series of the IFIX index, the Brazilian REIT market index, between 2021 and 2025. The validation results, obtained using two distinct methods, demonstrate that the model reproduces the main stylized facts observed in the real market: (i) the coverage rate of calibrated moments exceeds 75 percent; (ii) 96 percent of simulated trajectories are structurally indistinguishable from real IFIX periods according to the nearest-neighbor criterion; and (iii) stylized facts such as the power law of autocorrelations of absolute returns and aggregational Gaussianity emerge spontaneously, without being incorporated into the calibration objective function. The results of the validation process indicate that the artificial market captures structural dynamics of the FII market, opening perspectives for its use as a computational laboratory for the analysis of regulatory policies and pricing mechanisms.
tldr: This paper develops an agent-based artificial market for Brazilian Real Estate Investment Funds, focusing on financial market simulation rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to create a computational laboratory for analyzing regulatory policies and pricing mechanisms in the Brazilian REIT market.
method: They build a multi-agent system integrating the FII value chain, with heterogeneous investors (fundamentalist, speculator, noise trader) and endogenous macroeconomic variables, calibrated using the Method of Simulated Moments on historical IFIX index data.
result: The model reproduces stylized facts such as power-law autocorrelations of absolute returns and aggregational Gaussianity, with over 75% coverage of calibrated moments and 96% of trajectories indistinguishable from real data.
conclusion: The artificial market captures structural dynamics of the FII market and can serve as a tool for policy analysis.

title: SecDrift: Measuring Sector-Conditioned Security Drift In AI-Generated Code
authors: Dhivya Chandramouleeswaran Narayanaswami Natraj Bharadwaj
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25225v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLMs are increasingly used for code generation in critical infrastructure, yet the security effect of domain-specific prompting is understudied. We present SecDrift, a benchmark measuring sector-conditioned security drift: the change in static-analysis vulnerability rates when prompts are conditioned on industry contexts versus neutral baselines. We evaluate 7 LLMs (6 producing analyzable code) across 8 CISA critical infrastructure sectors and 9 CWE categories with 5 replicates (5,355 evaluations), using a 5-dimension transformation with a matched-baseline condition that holds the task fixed while substituting only domain terminology. Industry prompts naively appear more secure (14.0% vs. 11.4%, -2.7pp), but the gap is not statistically significant (Fisher's exact p = 0.24, Cohen's h = -0.08) and is a composition artifact of two CWE categories: excluding CWE-502 and CWE-22 eliminates and slightly reverses it (+0.4pp, p = 1.00). A mixed-effects logistic regression confirms sector identity is not a moderator and localizes the only detectable condition effect to those two vulnerability types. 0 of 8 sectors show drift distinguishable from baseline, corrected or uncorrected (|h| < 0.15). A placebo on two non-CISA sectors (e-commerce, online education) reproduces the CISA industry rate almost exactly (10.5% vs. 11.4%, p = 0.63): the small pooled pattern reflects generic industry-framing specificity, not critical-infrastructure identity. In contrast, model selection has a large and consistent effect: among full-output models vulnerability rates range from 11.6% to 16.1%, and these differences persist across conditions. Model choice, not prompt framing, is the more reliable security lever. We release the framework, prompts, generated code, findings, human-validation verdicts, and analysis scripts.
tldr: This paper studies security vulnerabilities in LLM-generated code across different industry sectors, finding that prompt framing has negligible effect compared to model choice.
motivation: LLMs are used for code generation in critical infrastructure, but the impact of domain-specific prompting on code security is not well understood.
method: The authors create a benchmark (SecDrift) that compares vulnerability rates in code generated with neutral vs. industry-conditioned prompts, using static analysis across 7 LLMs, 8 CISA sectors, and 9 CWE categories.
result: Industry prompts show a small, non-significant reduction in vulnerability rates (2.7pp), which is an artifact of two CWE categories; model choice has a much larger and consistent effect.
conclusion: Model selection is a more reliable lever for code security than prompt framing; sector-specific conditioning does not cause meaningful security drift.

title: Decision-Level Hijacking: Injecting Cognitive Bias Into Large Language Models Via Bit-Flip Attacks
authors: Yu Yan, Jiahao Chen, Siqi Lu, Yongjuan Wang, Ziming Zhao, Zhaoxuan Li, Tianyu Du, Qingjun Yuan, Shouling Ji
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25227v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have been widely applied in high-stakes decision-making scenarios such as corporate strategy, and users are increasingly relying on their outputs. However, the deep integration of open-source model sharing ecosystems with LLM-powered critical decision-making applications also introduces critical risks: if an attacker can manipulate the model's cognitive stance, they can indirectly influence the judgments and actions of downstream decision-makers. This paper defines such threats as decision-level hijacking. Existing attacks fail to achieve targeted cognitive manipulation without triggering prohibited content or degrading model functionality. To fill this gap, this paper reveals that Bit-Flip Attacks (BFAs) can serve as an attack vector for inducing decision-level hijacking, requiring no real-time interaction or control over the training process, and only a minimal number of weight bits need to be flipped after deployment to achieve stealthy, low-cost, and persistent cognitive manipulation. Therefore, we propose CogBias, a cognitive bias injection framework for LLMs. CogBias converts subjective preferences into optimization signals via a differentiable sentiment evaluator, uses a multi-objective loss to jointly constrain multiple dimensions, and constructs BitScout to locate critical bits, achieving targeted cognitive intervention under an ultra-sparse flip budget. Experiments on Llama-3.2-3B, Mistral-7B, and Qwen2.5-14B, as well as on the commercial recommendation and controversial factual topic scenarios, demonstrate that flipping only a small number of bits stably induces significant stance shifts on target topics, while the impact on non-target tasks and overall output distribution is limited. This work demonstrates that minute perturbations to low-level weight data suffice to undermine the high-level value alignment of LLMs.
tldr: This paper proposes a bit-flip attack framework to inject cognitive bias into LLMs for decision-level hijacking.
motivation: LLMs are used in high-stakes decisions, and attackers may manipulate their cognitive stance without triggering prohibited content or degrading functionality.
method: CogBias uses a differentiable sentiment evaluator to convert subjective preferences into optimization signals, multi-objective loss, and BitScout to locate critical bits for targeted cognitive intervention.
result: Flipping a small number of bits in Llama-3.2-3B, Mistral-7B, and Qwen2.5-14B induces significant stance shifts on target topics with limited impact on non-target tasks.
conclusion: Minute perturbations to low-level weight data can undermine high-level value alignment of LLMs, posing a security risk.

title: Hybrid Analysis For Secure Mcp Tool Use In Llm Agents
authors: Ping He, Yuexiang Xie, Yaliang Li, Shouling Ji
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25297v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid development of large language model (LLM) agents has enabled their broad adoption across diverse real-world tasks. To standardize interactions between LLM agents and external environments, Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools have emerged as a de facto standard and have been widely integrated into these systems. However, the use of MCP tools also introduces new safety risks, as LLM agents can be induced to perform malicious or unauthorized actions. Although prior work has proposed defenses for securing tool use in LLM agents, most methods rely on static analysis, i.e., inspecting prompts and generated outputs, which limits the defense effectiveness and robustness. To address these limitations, we propose MTGuard, a hybrid analysis-based defense framework designed to safeguard the use of MCP tools in LLM agents by leveraging lifecycle-aware static-dynamic co-analysis. Extensive evaluation demonstrates that MTGuard effectively mitigates multiple categories of harmful tool use across different LLM agents while maintaining performance on benign user tasks.
tldr: This paper proposes MTGuard, a hybrid analysis framework to secure MCP tool use in LLM agents.
motivation: LLM agents using MCP tools face safety risks from malicious actions, and existing static analysis defenses are limited.
method: MTGuard uses lifecycle-aware static-dynamic co-analysis to detect and mitigate harmful tool use.
result: Extensive evaluation shows MTGuard effectively mitigates multiple categories of harmful tool use across different LLM agents while maintaining benign task performance.
conclusion: Hybrid analysis improves security of LLM agent tool use without sacrificing utility.

title: SafeStats: Efficient 2pc Protocols For Data Statistic-Related Functions
authors: Tanren Liu, Xianjia Meng, Yang Liu, Xin Kang, Chenhui You, Yong Zeng, Zhuo Ma
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25430v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Statistical analysis on sensitive datasets like medical records and financial transactions is essential for decision-making, but raises significant privacy concerns. While existing secure Two-Party Computation (2PC) makes extensive efforts in designing the common secure primitives (e.g., addition and multiplication) or machine learning-related functions, few pay attention to the statistical functions. In this paper, we propose SafeStats, a secure toolkit tailored for 2PC secure statistical analysis. Specifically, to develop SafeStats, we first refer to Microsoft Excel's statistical library and summarize that most statistical operations can be achieved with three core functions:1) frequency counting, 2) sorting, and 3) non-linear math functions. Then, for each core statistical function, SafeStats presents an efficient 2PC implementation. For secure frequency counting, SafeStats adopts a secure shift-based strategy to avoid invoking expensive 2PC equality test protocols. For secure sort, SafeStats involves a secure segment-indicator protocol to achieve secure counting-based sort, which enables fast element sorting over specific statistical scenarios without the need for secure comparison. For non-linear math functions, we enhance the current reduce-then-approximate paradigm by introducing a bisection-based range reduction protocol. Finally, we implement SafeStats and test it on 14 common statistical analysis cases. As an example, for the chi-square test, SafeStats achieves a 1.5 [MATH] runtime speedup and a 4.2 [MATH] reduction in communication compared to directly using the current general-purpose 2PC library to realize it.
tldr: This paper presents efficient secure two-party computation protocols for statistical functions, focusing on privacy-preserving data analysis.
motivation: Statistical analysis on sensitive datasets raises privacy concerns, and existing secure computation tools lack efficient support for statistical functions.
method: The authors design SafeStats, a toolkit implementing secure frequency counting, sorting, and non-linear math functions using novel protocols like shift-based counting and segment-indicator sort.
result: SafeStats achieves significant speedups and communication reductions on common statistical tests, e.g., 1.5x runtime and 4.2x communication improvement for chi-square test.
conclusion: SafeStats demonstrates that tailored secure protocols can efficiently handle statistical functions, enabling practical privacy-preserving data analysis.

title: From Profiling To Parameterization: Physics-Guided Acoustic Eavesdropping Via Smartphone Accelerometers
authors: Guangyuan Ji, Wenjing Wang, Bingsheng Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25461v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present LEAKFORGE, a device-agnostic framework that converts cross-device accelerometer eavesdropping into a physics-guided data-generation problem. Crucially, device-specific leakage is not arbitrary; its dominant variation lies within a constrained family of audio-to-accelerometer transfer functions. LEAKFORGE samples this family to synthesize large-scale, device-diverse accelerometer traces from ordinary speech, explicitly modeling electromechanical transfer, structural resonances, filtering, and aliasing. An eavesdropping model trained entirely in this synthetic domain can then be applied directly to traces from previously unseen smartphones.
tldr: A framework for acoustic eavesdropping via smartphone accelerometers using physics-guided data generation.
motivation: To enable cross-device accelerometer-based speech eavesdropping without requiring per-device training data.
method: Models the audio-to-accelerometer transfer function family and synthesizes large-scale training data from ordinary speech.
result: The eavesdropping model trained on synthetic data works on previously unseen smartphones.
conclusion: Device-specific leakage can be parameterized and exploited for practical eavesdropping.

title: Architectural Backdoors In Vision-Language Model Supply Chains Via Representation Steering
authors: Maria Rosaria Briglia, Igor Maljkovic, Antonio Emanuele Cin\`a, Luca Oneto, Iacopo Masi, Fabio Roli
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25479v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision--Language Models (VLMs) are increasingly deployed through a model supply chain in which pretrained checkpoints, architecture definitions, text encoders, and exported computation graphs are distributed by third parties and reused across downstream services. This reuse model creates a security-critical trust boundary: VLM deployments inherit not only learned parameters but also executable behavior encoded in shared model artifacts. In this paper, we show that a malicious provider can exploit this trust boundary by embedding architectural backdoors into VLM supply chains through representation steering. Our attack introduces dormant steering logic into the model architecture through a trigger-gated additive modification of an intermediate representation, without poisoning training data, controlling downstream fine-tuning, or modifying prompts at deployment time. When the trigger is absent, the modification reduces to zero and the model follows its normal computation, preserving clean utility. When the trigger is present, a steering direction shifts the internal representation toward an attacker-defined objective. We evaluate the attack across multiple VLM families and downstream tasks, including visual question answering, text-to-image generation, retrieval, and semantic response biasing. The results show that the proposed architectural steering backdoor compromises integrity, safety enforcement, and ranking fairness while preserving normal behavior on clean inputs. We further show that shared VLM artifacts can carry dormant steering logic against downstream services, and we propose an auditing defense that inspects the executable logic distributed with model artifacts rather than only their learned weights.
tldr: This paper introduces architectural backdoors in vision-language model supply chains via representation steering, a security attack that does not involve quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper addresses security vulnerabilities in VLM supply chains where third-party artifacts can embed malicious behavior.
method: The attack adds trigger-gated steering logic to intermediate representations, remaining dormant without the trigger and shifting representations toward an attacker-defined objective when triggered.
result: The attack compromises integrity, safety, and fairness across multiple VLM tasks while preserving normal behavior on clean inputs.
conclusion: The work highlights the need for auditing defenses that inspect executable logic in model artifacts, not just learned weights.

title: Optimistic Verifiable Claims: A Blockchain Protocol For Conditionally Confidential Bidding In Decentralized Manufacturing
authors: Marko Corn, Nejc Ro\v{z}man, Primo\v{z} Podr\v{z}aj
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25517v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Decentralized manufacturing faces a pre-contractual impasse: a Provider cannot price a service accurately without inspecting the design file, yet the Consumer cannot share that file without exposing intellectual property. We introduce the Optimistic Verifiable Claim (OVC), a blockchain protocol that lets a Consumer publish a verifiable claim about a concealed design (such as the material it consumes) and a Provider price and bid on it without seeing the design. The claim is committed when the service is posted and stands unless the selected Provider challenges it; a challenge triggers a deterministic on-chain check that exposes any dishonesty, and the design is disclosed only to settle a dispute, never on the honest path. We implement four checks (authorized key access, delivery-channel integrity, syntactic conformance, and declared material consumption) in Solidity and measure them on a real 6.41 MB G-code file, the 3DBenchy, across Ethereum, Arbitrum, and opBNB. Every service incurs the cost of posting the encrypted design, with or without a dispute. For the 3DBenchy, the no-dispute outcome costs \[MATH]288 in 3 min on Arbitrum, and \[MATH]49,660 in up to 57 hours on Ethereum, \[MATH]19.73 in 13 min on opBNB. Costs and times grow with size: for a 50 MB industrial design, an undisputed service reaches \[MATH]22.36 and 16 min on opBNB, and a fully contested dispute reaches \[MATH]195 and 1.6 hours on opBNB. Of the four, the material-consumption check is the costliest, its predicate being the most expensive to evaluate on-chain. OVC makes confidential, claim-based bidding economically feasible on Arbitrum and opBNB, but not on Ethereum at industrial scale.
tldr: This paper proposes a blockchain protocol for confidential bidding in decentralized manufacturing, which is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: Decentralized manufacturing faces a pre-contractual impasse where providers need design information to price services, but consumers want to protect intellectual property.
method: The Optimistic Verifiable Claim (OVC) protocol allows consumers to publish verifiable claims about concealed designs, with on-chain checks triggered only if a provider challenges the claim.
result: The protocol is implemented and tested on Ethereum, Arbitrum, and opBNB, showing economic feasibility on Arbitrum and opBNB but not on Ethereum for industrial-scale designs.
conclusion: OVC enables confidential, claim-based bidding in decentralized manufacturing, but scalability and cost remain challenges on certain blockchains.

title: Kemeny Rank Aggregation Is NP-Hard For Three Voters
authors: Dominik Peters
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25540v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rank aggregation is the task of combining [MATH] input rankings (linear orders) of alternatives into a single output ranking. The Kemeny rank aggregation rule selects the output ranking that minimizes the total Kendall-tau distance to the input rankings, i.e., the total number of adjacent swaps that need to be performed across input rankings so that they are all equal to the output ranking. Dwork et al. (2001) proved that the problem of computing such a ranking is NP-complete for every even [MATH] and asked whether hardness holds even for [MATH]. We give a hardness reduction from MAX CUT that proves the problem is NP-complete for [MATH]. The reduction was found in July 2026 by GPT 5.6 Sol Ultra and simplified in part with help from Claude Fable 5.
tldr: This paper proves that Kemeny rank aggregation is NP-hard for three voters, using a reduction from MAX CUT.
motivation: The computational complexity of Kemeny rank aggregation was known to be NP-complete for even numbers of voters, but the case of three voters remained open. Resolving this question completes the complexity classification.
method: The authors construct a reduction from the MAX CUT problem to Kemeny rank aggregation with three voters, showing that finding an optimal ranking is NP-hard.
result: Kemeny rank aggregation is NP-complete for three voters, closing the open problem posed by Dwork et al. (2001).
conclusion: The problem is NP-complete for all numbers of voters except possibly one or two, where it is polynomial-time solvable.

title: Mapping CVEs To Mitre Att&ck Techniques: A Curated Gold-Set Classifier And The Limits Of LLM-Assisted Label Expansion
authors: Alexandre Dulaunoy C\'edric Bonhomme
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25572v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a reproducible pipeline for mapping Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) to MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise techniques from free-text vulnerability descriptions.
